raw:
I've built US-10-04 and committed it on `feature/US-10-04` as 646e392. Nothing was pushed (local run). The story's seven automated tests pass, run once more on that exact commit with a clean tree. The one gap is criterion #4: its real-model test, TC-10-19, is manual-only, so the merge is a human's call.

**What a user gets:**
- **Change sentences:** the model can now answer `change`, with the words naming the event and only what changes. "przesuń na 15" keeps the day and the length; a new day keeps the hour. A sentence read as a change never creates an event.
- **Which event changes:** if an event's details were open when the user went to the box, that event changes, whatever its date. Otherwise the app looks among events from today on, tolerating Polish word endings ("dentystę" finds "Dentysta").
- **Results:**
  - One event fits: its editor opens with the change made, and saving goes the usual way (series scope, asking about guests).
  - Several fit: they are listed under the box. Arrows and Enter pick one, Esc goes back to the text.
  - None fits: the box says "No such event found from today on" and keeps the text.
- **Events the user may not change** (read-only calendar, a guest without rights): their details stay open, unchanged, and say why. No editor opens and nothing is sent.

**The test set** gains 13 change sentences (7 Polish, 6 English), 43 in all. The fake-model test (TC-10-18) gives date 100 % and every field 91 %.

**Checked against the real model.** Ollama with `gemma4:e4b` was running on this machine, so I used it:
- The 13 recorded answers are what `gemma4:e4b` actually returned with the final rules.
- My first wording of the rules read "przesuń na 15" as 15 November, and it also broke 8 of the adding sentences. I reworded the rules and made the reading tolerate two quirks; a full re-run gave date 98 % and every field 95 %.

**Behaviour changes worth reviewing:**
- **DEC-231:** the model's answer is now taken in while an event's details are open (before, it waited for any window to close). So a new event described with details open opens its window in place of the details.
- **DEC-228:** a change applies only the day, the hour and the length. A title, guests or Meet in it are ignored, and an all-day event moves to the new day and stays all day.

**Manual checks left for the owner** (as the story's notes say): changing a real Google event with guests, one occurrence of a real series, and the list of matches in both themes.

One test fix to mention: TC-10-30 failed once under load because Save was clicked before the guests' free/busy answer resized the editor. It now waits for that answer, as the US-10-03 tests already do.
